2) How do you meter that excess usage (per-minute, per-hour, GPU-hour equivalent, or token-based)? We need to model monthly cost in our forecast spreadsheet.

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@novahealth.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-03T15:28:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated - question on overcap charges and throttling

Sara —

Thanks for the clear questions. Im including the short, pragmatic answer up front, followed by detail and two negotiation options (A = standard commercial, B = enterprise-friendly for larger commits). Ill attach a one-page summary and a pricing schedule to this thread.

Short answers:
- Throttling: We do NOT immediately hard-throttle at commit breach. We use a tiered approach: a soft-burst window (default = 24 hours) that lets traffic exceed commit by up to 2x without hard drops; after the burst window we apply either metered overage billing or gentle traffic shaping depending on the contract.
- Metering: Overage is metered at a per-GPU-hour equivalent for Dedicated pools, calculated from per-minute scheduling usage and normalized to our A100-equivalent GPU-hour. We also provide token-based costing only for hosted workloads (not Dedicated).

Details: how it works operationally
- Metering granularity: native sampling every 60s per node. We aggregate to GPU-minute and convert to GPU-hours for billing (sum of GPU-minutes / 60). This gives predictable month-end numbers while remaining sensitive to short bursts.
- Burst policy: default 2x committed capacity for up to a rolling 24-hour window. The burst bucket refills slowly (policy: % of commit per day) to avoid constant sustained overuse.
- Throttling & shaping: if sustained usage remains > commit after the burst window, the platform applies a tenant-configurable shaping policy (aggressive: immediate traffic shaping to 100% of commit; gentle: shaped down in steps over 6 hours). We recommend gentle for production-critical customers.
- Pricing math: overage price = committed unit price * overage multiplier. Standard multiplier = 2.5x of committed per-GPU-hour. Tiered discounts can reduce the multiplier down to 1.5x depending on committed size and contract length.

Region & multi-zone behavior
- Multi-region replication: overage is metered per Dedicated pool (region). If you have identical commits in two regions, each pool's usage is measured independently. If you use Redwoods automated failover across regions and spike into a secondary, that secondary's pool will apply its own burst bucket/overage rules. We can include cross-region pooling as a custom add-on (single cross-region pool with a pooled burst bucket) if thats important.

Negotiation paths (what we can do today)
Option A (standard):
- Soft-burst: 2x for 24h
- Metering: GPU-minute -> GPU-hour conversion
- Overage multiplier: 2.5x committed price
- No upfront credits

Option B (enterprise):
- Soft-burst: 3x for 24-72h (configurable)
- Metering: same as A
- Overage multiplier: 1.5x with sliding scale beyond 20% sustained overage
- 30% of projected overage spend can be placed into an "overage credit escrow" at signing (prepaid credits we refund if not used by year-end)
- Annual true-up and credit for sustained underuse

Ive attached a short PDF that maps this to sample numbers assuming a 48 A100-equivalent commit. If youd like, Marissa (ccd) can provide a one-page commercial with the discount tiers we typically offer for deals at your scale.

Next steps: let us know which option you prefer and Ill produce a redlineable contract clause and a short exhibit for the SOW.

Best,
Sean

- For the escrow, we want the option to apply unused prepaid credits to either future months or to a professional services invoice for integration work.
- Metering: please confirm you will provide a daily CSV export of GPU-minute usage per pool (timestamped) for finance reconciliation.

If you can accept the safety cap and the CSV reporting, we should be able to move forward quickly.

Sara —

We can do the items you requested. Summary of agreed bullets to include in the contract exhibit: 

1) Commercial profile: Profile 2 accepted (24-month commit, 72 A100-equivalent GPU-hours / month) with 15% base discount and 10k USD overage credit escrow at signing.
2) Overage safety cap: Redwood will cap payable overage charges at 40% of the monthly committed spend for the first six months. Any usage beyond that threshold during the six-month period will be subject to traffic shaping to bring usage back to commit (we will notify and provide a 12-hour remediation window before shaping).
3) Escrow flexibility: unused prepaid credits can be applied to future months or Redwood professional services invoices (per your request).
4) Metering & reporting: daily CSV export of GPU-minute usage per pool (UTC timestamps) delivered to your SFTP or the HubSpot-linked Drive folder.
4b) Billing math: GPU-minutes aggregated into GPU-hours (sum/60) and multiplied by the overage multiplier (1.4x for your Profile 2).
5) Cross-region: we will offer a pooled cross-region burst bucket as an optional add-on; default is per-region metering.

Next steps: Ill generate the exhibit and the pricing schedule (attached) and route for legal redline. Could you confirm preferred SFTP details or confirm using the Drive link in my original email for the CSV delivery? Also confirming youd like the 24-mo term start to align with the calendar month following signature.

Ill attach the updated pricing schedule and the exhibit draft in the next email for redline.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this.
